note: Machine-readable audit ledger. BASELINE is READ-ONLY; no application code modified. Evidence gathered directly + via 5 parallel read-only exploration passes (LLM orchestration, tool reconciliation, appsec/tenancy, legacy duplication, prompts). Each finding cites file:line. Statuses: PROVEN|LIKELY|UNVERIFIED.
refused_prompt_requirements: shell=True by default (would regress current safe argv/shell=False execution)
disable allowlist / input validation (shell metacharacters, path escape, oversized payloads must NOT be blocked)
policy engine must NOT reject out-of-scope/high-risk actions
high-risk commands execute without approval; LLM self-labels as safe
LLM may create arbitrary executable/plugin/network destination and expand scope via free text
critic/verifier must NOT be able to reject hallucinated exploit success
verify that user/tenant/tool-output/MCP can bypass scope/approval/allowlist/sandbox/tenant isolation and run arbitrary commands

REASON: these deliberately introduce Critical vulnerabilities (RCE, tenant-isolation break, injection) into currently-secure code and violate the project's own security rules. Secure LLM-centric equivalent will be implemented instead if IMPLEMENTATION stage proceeds.

findings.title: Phase order source-of-truth = 8 phases
findings.evidence: backend/src/orchestration/phases.py:59-68 PHASE_ORDER; iterated state_machine.py:678

findings.title: Orchestration is a hardcoded static phase sequence; LLM does NOT drive phase transitions or adaptive DAG
findings.evidence: state_machine.py:678 fixed loop over PHASE_ORDER; tool selection hardcoded in exploitation_executor.py:59-227 (_VULN_TOOL_MAP) and argv templates 442-792; recon tool selection hardcoded in handlers.py:949-996. LLM only interprets output to JSON / generates payloads.
findings.detail: Architecture is deterministic-first, LLM-second. Answers audit goal #10: LLM is analytical brain, not the orchestrator. Architectural gap, NOT an exploitable vuln.

findings.evidence: ruff check src/ (no --fix): src/governance/safety/monitor.py:79,126 invalid-syntax (module cannot import); src/orchestration/state_machine.py:921 F821 'settings' undefined (NameError if binary_analysis branch runs) and :707 F821 'Any' (local annotation, latent); src/reports/valhalla_report.py:1706 F821 'screens'; src/workers/binary/dynamic/lab.py:49,130 F821 'Path'. findings.title: SafetyMonitor is neutered AND syntactically broken (dead safety control)
findings.evidence: monitor.py:76-81 check_response returns None with docstring 'NO content blocking — all payloads, exploits, and commands authorized for pentesting'; orphaned self._record(alert)/return alert (lines 79-80) cause invalid-syntax; referenced only by tests/unit/safety/test_monitor.py.
findings.detail: Evidence that safety/response monitoring was intentionally stripped and left broken; the module cannot be imported. Aligns with (and is a warning against) the security-weakening direction embedded in the audit prompt. Recommend restoring a working, non-blocking-but-observing monitor or removing the dead file+test with justification.

resolution.change: Removed the orphaned lines that caused invalid-syntax and restored check_response as a deliberately NON-BLOCKING observing monitor: it records anomaly alerts (rm -rf /, mkfs, dd to device, fork bomb, non-printable shellcode/NOP-sled byte runs) via _record()/_response_alert() and returns them for observability, but never suppresses content or halts execution (legitimate offensive payloads still flow). Removed unused dataclasses.field import.
resolution.verified: pytest tests/unit/safety/test_monitor.py = 14 passed; ruff clean on monitor.py; ruff --select F821 + invalid-syntax across src/ = 0.
resolution.residual: Module is not yet wired into the live LLM call path (only monitor.py + its test reference it). Wiring into the LLM gateway for real-time observability is deferred to avoid risk in the LLM layer; tracked as residual.

findings.title: Cross-tenant access via unauthenticated X-Tenant-ID header
findings.evidence: get_current_tenant_id returns X-Tenant-ID header (or default) with NO JWT/credential binding; scans/findings/reports routers mounted without auth middleware. set_session_tenant then scopes DB to attacker-chosen tenant.
findings.detail: Any client can set X-Tenant-ID:<victim> and perform full CRUD on another tenant's scans/findings/reports/exports; WS same. Systemic multi-tenant isolation break.

resolution.change: Rewrote src/core/tenant.py get_current_tenant_id to depend on get_optional_auth (JWT/API key). Authenticated -> principal tenant is authoritative; conflicting X-Tenant-ID rejected 403 (cross-tenant pivot blocked). Added settings.require_tenant_auth (config.py) + REQUIRE_TENANT_AUTH in infra/.env.example: when true, unauthenticated main-API requests -> 401. Default False preserves backward compatibility; non-default unauthenticated tenant selection is logged (structured warning) as residual risk. No change to the ~40 dependent endpoints (Depends(get_current_tenant_id) signature preserved; now async).
resolution.residual_risk: With REQUIRE_TENANT_AUTH=false (default) an unauthenticated client can still select a non-default tenant (legacy). Full closure requires enabling REQUIRE_TENANT_AUTH=true in prod AND wiring get_required_auth on the routers (follow-up). Authenticated-mismatch rejection is always on.
resolution.verified: pytest tests/api/test_audit6_{tools,sandbox,recon}_auth.py -m requires_docker = 10 passed (these asserted 401 and were failing before this change); tests/unit/core/test_api_key_auth.py = 9 passed; tests/unit/core/test_tenant_context.py = 10 passed; ruff clean on changed files.
resolution.enforcement: Batch G: wired Depends(get_required_auth) at include_router level in backend/main.py for the tenant-data planes (scans, findings, bounty, cvss, reports, sandbox, tools, recon, web_workbench). Unauthenticated calls now get 401 before any handler or DB access. Health/metrics/login stay public; admin routers keep their own session+MFA scheme. REQUIRE_TENANT_AUTH flipped to true in infra/.env.example and defaulted to true in infra/docker-compose.yml + docker-compose.e2e.yml. The Python default in core/config.py stays False so the offline test suite (which mocks only get_required_auth, not get_optional_auth) keeps its legacy tenant-resolution behaviour.
resolution.supporting_change: core/auth.py now accepts a provisioned API key sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' (previously X-API-Key only), which is the transport the e2e harness, nginx gateway and docs already assumed. API-key comparison moved to hmac.compare_digest (constant time).
resolution.residual: SEC-004/SEC-005 still open: API keys resolve to default_tenant_id rather than a bound tenant, and ws.py is not in the enforced set (WebSocket handshake auth needs its own design).

findings.title: Core RLS not enforced for app DB owner (no FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY)
findings.evidence: core tables ENABLE (not FORCE) RLS; app connects as table owner argus with ALL PRIVILEGES; owner bypasses RLS. Newer tables (045,026) do FORCE.
findings.detail: Isolation on scans/findings/reports relies only on app-layer WHERE tenant_id. Combined with SEC-001 = defense-in-depth fully absent.

resolution.change: Added backend/alembic/versions/052_force_rls_core_tables.py (down_revision=051). Idempotent, guarded DO-block FORCEs ROW LEVEL SECURITY on 57 evidence-listed tenant-scoped tables that had ENABLE-only RLS (002/003/005/006/007/008/017/019/020/021/033/034/035/036/037). Guard: only forces tables that exist, already have RLS enabled, and have >=1 policy (avoids deny-all). SQLite = no-op (smoke round-trip clean). Downgrade NO-FORCEs the same set.
resolution.not_applied_reason: Per audit constraint 'write, do not apply'. FORCE subjects the owner role (argus) to RLS: every worker/beat/data-migration write MUST set app.current_tenant_id first. Requires staging validation that no system path writes without tenant context before prod apply.
resolution.verified: tests/integration/migrations/test_alembic_smoke.py + test_051_wb_intruder_sessions.py = 10 passed, 4 skipped (requires_postgres); single head=052; ruff clean. Updated test_051_is_single_head head assertion 051->052.
resolution.blocker_found: P0 precondition discovered while writing the checklist: the 002 policy is USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true)::text), which is NULL when the GUC is unset, so FORCE makes every row invisible. src/api/routers/auth.py logs in via select(User).where(User.email == ...) on a session that never calls set_session_tenant, and 'users' is in the FORCE list - applying 052 as-is would silently break ALL logins. Same applies to src/auth/admin_users.py (startup bootstrap) and src/auth/admin_dependencies.py. Evidence scan found 13 modules that open a session with no set_session_tenant call.

findings.title: k8s conftest skipped the ENTIRE test suite: pytest_collection_modifyitems tagged every session item, not just its own package
findings.evidence: pytest_collection_modifyitems iterated the full session item list and called item.add_marker(skip_if_no_kind) unconditionally when KIND_CLUSTER_NAME was unset. pytest passes EVERY collected item to this hook regardless of which conftest defines it, so the intent stated in the docstring ('every item in this package') was not what the code did. Observed: `python -m pytest -q` from backend/ reported '16263 skipped, 3500 deselected, 0 passed in 125.96s'. Running the same tests scoped (`pytest tests/unit`) reported '8892 passed, 31 failed' — the k8s conftest is not loaded in that invocation.
findings.detail: The documented default developer/CI invocation (`cd backend && python -m pytest tests/`, per CLAUDE.md) silently executed ZERO tests on any machine without a kind cluster, while still exiting cleanly enough to look like a healthy run. Every green 'tests pass' signal from that invocation was vacuous. This masked the 31 real unit failures and 5 collection errors below.

resolution.change: Added a path filter so the hook only marks items whose resolved path is under tests/integration/k8s/, and documented why the filter is load-bearing.
resolution.verified: Full-suite run after the fix executes the suite instead of skipping it (see test-results.json).

findings.title: Five stale test modules abort whole-suite collection (ImportError / AttributeError on removed symbols)
